newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks ride up at open on Dow rebound.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks ride up at open on Dow rebound.

text.p: Australian stocks took a ride higher at the opening on Wednesday on the back of a mild rebound on Wall Street, with resources heavyweights CRA and BHP heading the pack, but trade was quiet, brokers said.
At 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 10.1 points up at 2,362.3 points, but seven points off its morning high.
Brokers said there was still some nervousness in the local market due to the big sell-off in U.S. stocks over Easter and as the local market drifted from its record high in mid-February.
"The recovery seems to be following through here," said Mark Pervan, a broker at Daiwa Securities.

The rebound in the local market did not make much of a dent in the 70 point fall on Tuesday following the 290 point drop in New York over the Easter holiday weekend on concerns about further interest rate hikes.
"I think people have still got a wait-and-see attitude and they will probably be buying selectively," Pervan said.

The biggest trade was in Anglo-Australian miner CRA with just under A$25 million (US$19.6 million) traded. Most of the major morning trade was in the resource sector following the firmer base metal prices in London.
Most of the blue-chip shares were in repair mode today after Tuesday's big sell-off, brokers said.

The banks which fell over two percent on Tuesday as local bond yields rose, were amongst the major risers today, with National Australia Bank and and Commonwealth Bank both up 0.8 percent, mirroring a slight rebound on local bond yields.
The rebound was across the board, except for the infrastructure, transport, contractors and telecommunications sectors which all went against the rising trend.
